Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:11:1.hebrew: רובע שקל - מטבע קטן של חצי דינר, והוא הקרוי בגמרא סלע מדינה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:11:1.english: A quarter of a shekel - A small coin of half a dinar, and it is what is called in the Gemara a provincial sela [sela medinah].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:12:1.english: Why [does he need] to make a dinar dependent on a shekel - Let him say [regarding] a dinar: up to half a zuz.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:12:2.english: That comes from a shekel - If the shekel diminished to half [its weight] and became a dinar.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:13:1.english: It is permitted to maintain it - And to spend it as a dinar.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:13:2.hebrew: דינר הבא מסלע אסור לקיימו - אפי' להוציאו בדינר, דמתוך שהוא בא ממטבע עבה ורחבה, טועין בו לאמדו בשקל ואתי לקבולי בתורת שקל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:13:2.english: A dinar that comes from a sela, it is prohibited to keep it - Even to spend it as a dinar, because since it comes from a thick and wide coin, [people] err regarding it, estimating it as a shekel, and [one] will come to accept it as a shekel.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:14:1.hebrew: מאי קאמר - הא ליכא למימר "פחות מיכן" — דאם עמד סלע על פחות משקל או אם עמד דינר על פחות מרובע — איסר, אסור לקיימו. דמאי איריא איסר? אפילו משהו נמי! דהא אמר בסלע "עד שקל", ותו לא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:14:1.english: What is [the tanna] saying - For one cannot say [that the baraita means] "less than this" — [namely,] that if a sela stood at less than a shekel, or if a dinar stood at less than a rova — [by] an issar, it is forbidden to keep it; for why specify an issar? Even a slight amount [would] also [be forbidden], for [the tanna] already stated regarding a sela, "up to a shekel," and no more.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:14:2.hebrew: יתר מכדי אונאתה - לר"מ כדאית ליה, לרבי יהודה כדאית ליה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:14:2.english: Greater than the measure of its exploitation - For Rabbi Meir according to his [view], [and] for Rabbi Yehuda according to his [view].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:14:3.english: Prohibited to spend it - as a good [coin].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:15:1.hebrew: טמאה - מקבלת טומאה מעתה, שהרי עשאה כלי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:15:1.english: Impure - [It] is susceptible to ritual impurity from now on, for he has made it into a vessel.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:15:2.hebrew: יקוץ - יחתכנה לשנים, דאתי לאפוקה בשקל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:15:2.english: He must cut [it] - He must cut it in two, lest he come to spend it as a shekel.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:16:1.english: [If it eroded] more than that, he may keep [it] - For relative to a sela, its deficiency is noticeable, and it will not be confused with a sela.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:1:1.english: Eight pundeyon - [This is] one-sixth, like other [cases of] overcharging.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:2:1.hebrew: בכרכים - שיש שם שולחני, עד כדי שיראה לשולחני:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:2:1.english: In the cities - Where there is a money changer, [one may return it] until he can show [it] to a money changer.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:2:2.english: In the villages - Because there is no money changer there.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:2:3.hebrew: עד ערבי שבתות - שבא להוציאה בערב שבת לסעודת שבת, אז ידע אם יוכל להוציאה ויקבלוה ממנו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:2:3.english: Until Shabbat eves - For he comes to spend it on Shabbat eve for the Shabbat meal; then he will know whether he can spend it and [whether] they will accept it from him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:2:4.english: And if [he] was - [That is,] the one who gave [it] recognizes it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:2:5.hebrew: אפילו לאחר י"ב חודש כו' - בגמרא פריך, הא אמרת עד ערבי שבתות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:2:5.english: Even after twelve months, etc. - In the Gemara, it asks: Did you not say "until Shabbat eves"?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:2:6.english: And he has only a grievance against him - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:3:1.hebrew: ונותנה - בחילול מעשר שני, ובגמ' מפרש אם בשויה, אם בסלע יפה. לפי שאינה מדה זו של פוסלי מטבע בשביל חסרון מעט, אלא נפש רעה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:3:1.english: And one may give it - For the redemption of second tithe, and in the Gemara it explains whether [it is given] at its [actual] value or as a full-value sela; [this is permitted] because this practice of those who disqualify a coin on account of a slight deficiency is nothing other than a miserly soul.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:4:1.hebrew: ורמינהי כמה תהא סלע חסירה ויהא בה אונאה - אלמא בהני שיעורי הויא אונאה, ומתני' קתני: "ולא יהא", אלמא בהני שיעורי לאו אונאה היא עד דאיכא טפי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:4:1.english: And [the Gemara] raises a contradiction: How much may a sela be deficient and there be exploitation in it - Apparently, with these measures it is [considered] exploitation, whereas our Mishnah teaches: "and there shall not be [exploitation]" — apparently, with these measures it is not exploitation until there is more [deficiency].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:5:1.hebrew: אמר רב פפא - לעולם אימא לך: בהני שיעורי הויא אונאה, ו"לא יהא" דמתני' לאו אשיעורא קאי, אלא אפחות מכשיעור קאי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:5:1.english: Rav Pappa said - In fact, I can tell you [that] at these measures it is [considered] exploitation, and [the phrase] "there shall not be [exploitation]" of our mishna does not refer to the [exact] measure, rather it refers to less than the measure.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:5:2.hebrew: מלמטה למעלה קחשיב - וה"ק: סלע הפוחתת והולכת, עד כמה יכול להוציאה? עד שתפחת שיעור כך וכך, ומכיון שהגיעה לשיעור הזה, יהא בה אונאה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:5:2.english: He calculates from low to high - And this is what he is saying: [Regarding] a sela that is progressively depreciating, up to how much may one spend it? Until it depreciates [by] such-and-such an amount, and once it reaches this amount, there is exploitation in [using] it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:5:3.english: And the external Tanna - Who uses [the expression] "and there is [exploitation] in it."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:5:4.hebrew: מלמעלה למטה חשיב - סלע שפחתה, כמה פחתה להיות בה אונאה — מפרש כל פחיתה גדולה שבה, כגון שבע איסרות, או שש, או חמש, הויא אונאה עד ד', והיא בכלל. אבל לתנא דידן, אין ארבעה בכלל "לא יהא", ועל כרחך לא מיתוקמא אלא בהכי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:5:4.english: [He] calculates from high to low - [Regarding] a sela that has depreciated — how much must it depreciate for there to be ona'ah [exploitation] in it? [The external tanna] specifies every large depreciation in it: for example, seven issars, or six, or five, is ona'ah, down to four [issars], and [four] is included. However, according to our tanna, four [issars] are not included in "there is no [ona'ah]." And perforce, [the matter] can only be established in this way.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:6:1.hebrew: ומאי שנא בטלית - סתם סחורה, דתנן בהו לעיל (בבא מציעא דף מט:) שתות למקח:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:6:1.english: And what is different with regard to a garment - [This refers to] ordinary merchandise, regarding which we learned in the Mishnah above (Bava Metzia 49b) [that exploitation is] one-sixth of the purchase [price].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:7:1.hebrew: ר"ש היא - דגבי סלע אית ליה שתות:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:7:1.english: It is Rabbi Shimon - For regarding a sela, he holds [it is] one-sixth.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:7:2.hebrew: עשיק לגביך - הצריך לכסות גופך וגביך, קנה ביוקר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:7:2.english: Overpay for your back - That which is needed to cover your body and your back, buy at a high price.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:7:3.hebrew: ושוי לכריסך - למאכלך, לא תקנה אלא בשווין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:7:3.english: And [acquire] at cost for your stomach - For your food, do not buy except at its [true] value.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:7:4.hebrew: עשיק - לשון יוקר הוא, וחבירו באיזהו נשך (לקמן בבא מציעא דף עד.): באתרא דאמימר עשיק עפרא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:7:4.english: Ashik - It is an expression of expensiveness, and its parallel is in [the chapter] Eizehu Neshekh (below, Bava Metzia 74a): "In Ameimar's locale, earth is expensive [ashik afra]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:7:5.english: Since it does not circulate for him - That it does not pass in spending.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:8:1.hebrew: יתר על כן מוכרה בשוויה - לקמיה מפרש לה: יתירה על כן, שלא פחתה כדי אונאה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:8:1.english: [If it is] more than that, he sells it at its value - Further on, [the Gemara] explains it: [it means] more than that, [i.e.,] that it has not diminished by the amount of ona'ah [monetary exploitation].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:8:2.english: He sells it for its value - [In exchange] for a good sela.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:9:1.hebrew: בסלע עד שקל - סלע הטבוע ופוחת והולך עד שקל, מותר לקיימו, שאין עשוי לרמות בו בני אדם למוכרו בסלע יפה, לפי שפחת שלו ניכר. אבל משפחת משקל, לא יקיימנו, לפי שבא לרמות ולמוכרו בתורת שקל, שאין פחת שלו ניכר לגבי שקל — מתוך שהוא רחב, שבתחילה היה סלע, אינו נראה חסר משקל. שקל הוא מטבע של חצי סלע, ודינר מטבע קטן, שנים מהם יש בשקל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:9:1.english: With regard to a sela, until a shekel - A minted sela that progressively erodes down to a shekel is permitted to be kept, for it is not apt to be used to deceive people by passing it off as a good sela, because its erosion is noticeable. However, once it has eroded below a shekel, one may not keep it, because he [might] come to deceive [others] and pass it off as a shekel, since its erosion is not noticeable relative to a shekel — because it is wide, having originally been a sela, it does not appear to be less than a shekel. A shekel is a coin [worth] half a sela, and a dinar is a small coin, two of which make a shekel.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:9:2.hebrew: בדינר עד רובע - ואם היה דינר נפחת עד שעמד על רובע, מותר לקיימו. קס"ד רובע דינר קאמר, ולקמיה פריך: מאי שנא סלע דלא מצי לשהויי אלא עד חציו, ודינר עד רובע? משחסר ועמד על פחות מרובע, לא יקיימנו, דאתי לאפוקיה ברובע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:9:2.english: With regard to a dinar, until one-quarter - And if a dinar eroded until it stood at a quarter, it is permitted to keep it. We initially assumed [the Mishnah] means a quarter of a dinar, and later [the Gemara] asks: What is the difference [between] a sela, which one may not keep except until half of it, and a dinar, [which one may keep] until a quarter? Once it is deficient and stands at less than a quarter, he may not keep it, lest he come to spend it as a quarter.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:9:3.english: Less than that, an issar, [it is] prohibited - [The Gemara] explains [this] further on.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:9:4.hebrew: לא ימכרנה - זו שאמרו אסור לקיימה, לא התירו לו שימכרנה בדמיה לא לתגר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:9:4.english: He may not sell it - [Regarding] this [coin] of which they said it is forbidden to keep it, they did not permit him to sell it for its value — not to a merchant.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:9:5.english: Nor to a charam - A coercive man.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:9:6.english: Nor to a murderer - A murderer.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 52a:9:7.english: That they deceive others with it - And out of fear [people] will accept it from their hand as a good [coin].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:11:1.hebrew: ולא קתני עד רביע - ואע"ג דרובע מצי למהוי נמי רובע דינר, כדתנן בפ"ק דכריתות (דף ח.): "בו ביום עמדו ברבעתיים", והיינו רובע דינר כדפי' התם, וכן אמרינן התם: "גר שנתגייר צריך שיפריש רובע לקינו"; מ"מ אי מיירי הכא ברובע דינר, ה"ל למיתני רביע, דלא נטעי ברובע שקל:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:11:1.english: And does not teach "up to revia" - Even though rova can also be a quarter [rova] of a dinar — as we learned in the Mishnah in the first chapter of Keritot (8a): "On that day they stood at two quarters [riv'atayim]," and that means a quarter of a dinar, as [Rashi] explained there; and similarly we say there: "A convert who converts must set aside a quarter [rova] for his bird-offering" — nevertheless, if [the baraita] were dealing here with a quarter of a dinar, it should have taught revia, so that we would not err [and think it refers] to a quarter of a shekel.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:14:1.hebrew: אמר אביי פחתה סלע יותר מכדי אונאה איסר אסור להוציאה - פרש"י: ביפה. וא"ת: פשיטא, ורבא נמי שהקשה "אפילו משהו נמי", היה לו להקשות "אפי' כדי אונאה נמי"? וי"ל: דמיירי אפי' בדעתו להחזיר האונאה — אסור, כיון דהמקח טעות הוא; אבל כדי אונאה — מותר להוציאה ביפה, ובלבד שיחזיר האונאה אם יתבענו הלה קודם שיראה לשולחני, ומותר כיון שהמקח מתקיים. ופחות מכדי אונאה — מוכרה ביפה, אפילו אם אין דעתו להחזיר אונאה, משום דהוי לאלתר מחילה. "רבא אמר פחתה איסר לדינר" — אסור להוציאה ביפה אם אין דעתו להחזיר, משום דהוי אונאה כר"מ. ועוד יש לפרש: "אמר אביי כו'" — אסור להוציאה אפילו בשויה, וסבר כמ"ד בסמוך: "יתר על כן יקוץ", אבל פחות מאיסר שרי, דלהפסד מרובה חששו ולא להפסד מועט. ורבא דקאמר "אפי' משהו נמי" — לית ליה האי סברא, ומצי נמי סבר רבא בין כמ"ד יקוץ בין כמ"ד יקיים:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:14:1.english: Abaye said: If a sela eroded by an issar more than the measure of exploitation, it is prohibited to spend it - Rashi explained: at its full value [i.e., as a good coin]. And if you will say: [Is this not] obvious? And Rava too, who objected, "Even any amount as well," should have objected, "Even the measure of exploitation as well"! And one can answer: [The baraita] is speaking [of a case where] even if he intends to return the exploitation, it is prohibited, since it is a mistaken transaction [and thus void]; however, [if it eroded by] the exact measure of exploitation, it is permitted to spend it at its full value, provided that he returns the exploitation if the other party claims it from him before he shows it to a moneychanger, and it is permitted since the transaction stands. And [if it eroded by] less than the measure of exploitation, he may sell it at its full value, even if he does not intend to return [any] exploitation, because it is an immediate waiver [of the claim]. "Rava said: If it eroded by an issar per dinar" — it is prohibited to spend it at its full value if he does not intend to return [the difference], because it constitutes exploitation in accordance with Rabbi Meir. And there is another way to explain: "Abaye said, etc." — it is prohibited to spend it even at its [actual] value, and he holds like the one who says immediately below: "More than that, he must cut it," whereas less than an issar is permitted, for [the Sages] were concerned about a significant loss and not about a small loss. And Rava, who says "Even any amount as well," does not hold this reasoning, and Rava could also hold like either the one who says "he must cut it" or the one who says "he may keep it."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:15:1.hebrew: והתקינה - אם צריכה מעשה, כמו חיתוך, אתי שפיר דנקט "התקינה", דמידי דמחוסר מלאכה אין טמא במחשבה, כדאמרינן במרובה (ב"ק דף סו:); ואי אינה צריכה חיתוך, הוי "התקינה" לאו דוקא, דכל הכלים יורדים לידי טומאתם במחשבה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:15:1.english: And he prepared it - If it requires a [physical] action, such as cutting, it works out well that [the Mishnah] used [the term] "he prepared it," for something that is lacking work does not become susceptible to ritual impurity through thought [alone], as we say in [the chapter] Merubeh (Bava Kamma 66b); and if it does not require cutting, "he prepared it" is not exact, for all vessels become susceptible to ritual impurity through thought [alone]:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:16:1.hebrew: יתר על כן יקוץ - "ולא ימכרנו לתגר" מצי נמי קאי אפחתה יתר מכדי אונאתה, וה"פ: אפילו ע"מ לנוקבה לא ימכרנו לתגר ולחרס, אבל לאחרים ימכור על מנת לנוקבה. ולמ"ד "יתר על כן יקיים", "לא ימכרנה לתגר" לא קאי אלא אבסלע עד שקל, דאמר פחתה יותר משקל אפילו פרוטה אסור לקיימה, ואהא קאי "לא ימכרנה לתגר" כו':
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:16:1.english: [If it eroded] more than that, he must cut [it] - [The ruling] "and he may not sell it to a merchant" can also refer to [a coin that] eroded more than its measure of exploitation, and this is its explanation: Even on condition to pierce it, he may not sell it to a merchant or to a robber, but to others he may sell [it] on condition to pierce it. And according to the one who says "[if it eroded] more than that, he may maintain [it]," "he may not sell it to a merchant" refers only to [the statement] "for a sela, up to a shekel," where it says [that if] it eroded more than a shekel [even by] a perutah, it is forbidden to maintain it; and to this [case] refers "he may not sell it to a merchant," etc.:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:1:1.hebrew: שני פונדיונים לדינר - והא דלא אמר מעה לדינר, משום דרבי יהודה נקט פונדיון קאמר איהו שני פונדיונים. וא"ת, תקשה לרב דאמר שתות מקח שנינו ולא שתות מעות, דהכא לר' שמעון, אם מכר סלע שוה כ' מעות בכ"ד הוי אונאה, והיינו שוה ה' בו' דהוי לרב ביטול מקח, ובגמ' מוקי מתני' דלעיל כר' שמעון; ואפי' לשמואל דאמר שתות מעות שנינו תקשה, דבשתות מקח מודה דהוי נמי אונאה, וה"ק: ב' פונדיונות לדינר הוי אונאה, אבל ב' פונדיונות פחות פרוטה הוי מחילה, אע"ג דאכתי הוי שתות מקח. וי"ל, דמיירי שמכר לו טלית שוה כ"ד מעות בסלע, ונתן לו סלע שחסר ד' מעות, דהיינו שתות מקח. מיהו לעיל פי' טעם דמ"ד שתות מקח, לפי שהאונאה והטעות תלוי בחפץ שצריך שומא ולא במעות, והכא הטעות והאונאה הוי בסלע:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:1:1.english: Two pundeyonot per dinar - And [the reason] he did not say "a ma'ah per dinar" [is] because Rabbi Yehudah [in the Mishnah] mentioned pundeyon, he [too] says "two pundeyonot." And if you ask: This poses a difficulty for Rav, who says we learned [in the Mishnah] a sixth of the purchased item [is ona'ah] and not a sixth of the money — for here, according to Rabbi Shimon, if one sold a sela worth twenty ma'ot for twenty-four [ma'ot], it is ona'ah, and that is [selling something] worth five for six, which according to Rav is a voiding of the sale, yet in the Gemara it establishes the Mishnah above in accordance with Rabbi Shimon! And even according to Shmuel, who says we learned a sixth of the money, it poses a difficulty, for regarding a sixth of the purchased item he concedes that it is also ona'ah, and this is what [the Mishnah] is saying: two pundeyonot per dinar is ona'ah, but two pundeyonot minus a perutah is waived, even though it is still a sixth of the purchased item! And one can answer that it is dealing with [a case] where he sold him a cloak worth twenty-four ma'ot for a sela, and he gave him a sela that was lacking four ma'ot, which is a sixth of the purchased item. However, above [it was] explained that the reason of the one who says "a sixth of the purchased item" is because the ona'ah and the error depend on the object, which requires appraisal, and not on the money; whereas here, the error and the ona'ah are in the sela [itself]:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:5:1.hebrew: תנא דידן קחשיב מלמטה למעלה - דאין אונאה עד ד' איסרין ולא עד בכלל, דבד' איסרין יש אונאה; דבגמרא אמרינן: "מאן תנא טלית? ר"ש היא, דאמר ח' פונדיונין הויין אונאה":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:5:1.english: Our Tanna calculates from below to above - That there is no ona'ah [overcharging] up to four issars, and not including [four issars], for at four issars there is ona'ah; as in the Gemara we say: "Who is the Tanna [who taught the case of] a garment? It is R. Shimon, who said [that] eight pundions constitute ona'ah."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:5:2.hebrew: ותנא ברא קחשיב מלמעלה למטה - אי גרסינן בברייתא "עד כמה", אתי שפיר דחשיב מלמעלה למטה, וסבר עד ועד בכלל. אבל אי לא גרסינן "עד", לא הוה צריך למימר דחשיב מלמעלה למטה, אלא כמשמעו: "כמה יהא אונאה? ד' איסרין". ואגב דקאמר לתנא דידן "מלמטה למעלה", נקט לתנא ברא "מלמעלה למטה":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:5:2.english: And the external tanna calculates from high to low - If we read [the text] in the baraita [as] "until how much," it works out well that he calculates from high to low and holds [that the word] "until" [means] inclusive. However, if we do not read "until," he would not have needed to say that he calculates from high to low; rather, [it is] according to its plain meaning: "How much is [considered] exploitation? Four issars." And on account of saying regarding our tanna "from low to high," he [also] used [the expression] "from high to low" regarding the external tanna.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:7:1.hebrew: עשיק לגביך - וא"ת: התינח נתאנה לוקח, נתאנה מוכר מאי איכא למימר? והתינח כסות, פירות מאי איכא למימר? וי"ל דלא פלוג רבנן. ועי"ל דעיקר הטעם הוי "סלע, כיון דלא סגי, לא מחיל":
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 52a:7:1.english: Overpay for your back - And if you say: This works well [when] the buyer was overcharged, [but when] the seller was defrauded, what is there to say? And this works well [for] a garment, [but for] produce, what is there to say? And one can answer that the Rabbis did not differentiate [between cases]. And furthermore, one can answer that the main reason [for the distinction] is: "A sela, since it does not circulate, he does not waive [it]."
